title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's sequel to 'La Longue Marche' (variations on the loop equation, c. 1981). He is building, from a profinite group 𝔊 with subgroups 𝔊^♮ ⊂ 𝔊^{**} and a subgroup L_0, a group Z_{ρ,σ} (the transcription's ξ is very likely ρ). Z_{ρ,σ} is an extension of Γ_{ρ,σ} and maps (70) to a 'Borel' group B_0' of matrices (μ λ; 0 1) with μ ∈ Ẑ*. The previous page sets up the subgroup Z_{ρ,σ}(o), the inverse image of the diagonal torus T_0' (λ = 0). The hoped-for hypothesis is that Z_{ρ,σ}(o) ∩ L_0^♮ = 1 and Z_{ρ,σ}(o) → Γ_{ρ,σ} is an isomorphism, i.e. Z = Z(o)·L_0^♮ (a semidirect-product splitting). On this page he notes three things.
(1) Z(o) has the good property of being functorial in an evident sense, which he regards as essential for a good formalism.
(2) This lets him define a subgroup (G_{ρ,σ})_0 ⊂ G^♮_{ρ,σ} via (68). If that definition proves too restrictive, a 'finer' definition would be the right one and would deserve the simpler notation G^♮_{ρ,σ}.
(3) Alternative approach: drop the ad hoc restrictions in the definition of Z_{ρ,σ}. Those restrictions are what force L_0^♮ = L_0 ∩ 𝔊^♮, i.e. for l ∈ L_0, (int(l),1,1,1) ∈ Z ⇔ l ∈ 𝔊^♮. Counterexample in the universal case, where 𝔊^♮ = Π_0: take l = l_0. Its image in 𝔊^{**}/𝔊^♮ = 𝔊/Π_0 is the nontrivial central element. The inner automorphism it induces on 𝔊^+/Π_0 (and on 𝔊/Π_0) is trivial. So conjugation cannot detect membership in 𝔊^♮, and without the restrictions the desired exactness property fails.
He then judges it premature to dissect the groups G^♮_{ρ,σ}, M^♮_{ρ,σ}. The next page says gross errors of orientation may remain, to be corrected by examining special cases. He therefore suspends this line of investigation, to revisit it in §48 XI.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The argument in (3) is a valid counterexample: a central element acts trivially by conjugation, so the 'iff' cannot hold without the restrictions. It shows the alternative approach fails rather than containing a mistake. The constructions are explicitly provisional and the author himself suspects orientation errors.

ideas.what: Subgroup Z_{ρ,σ}(o) as inverse image of the torus T_0' ⊂ B_0' (matrices (μ 0; 0 1), μ ∈ Ẑ*), hoped to be a section, giving Z = Z(o)·L_0^♮, functorial
ideas.modern_name: splitting of an extension via inverse image of a maximal torus in a Borel of GL_2(Ẑ); a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group construction
ideas.usually_credited_to: related GT-group work: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; general context in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Central element l_0 with trivial inner action shows int-restriction cannot characterize L_0 ∩ 𝔊^♮
ideas.modern_name: kernel of G → Out/Aut detecting the center

missed.claim: Grothendieck abandons, provisionally, the construction of refined groups G^♮_{ρ,σ}, M^♮_{ρ,σ} attached to the loop equation. He defers it to §48 XI pending study of special cases.
missed.quote: Mais peut-être est-il prématuré d'essayer déjà de "disséquer" ces groupes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are variant Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type groups with torus-section conditions. Their status relative to modern GT variants (e.g. Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura) is unclear, but the page is too provisional to extract a result.

deep.surprise_reason: Working notes of a provisional construction that the author himself abandons. The counterexample is elementary, and no finished, uncredited result appears.
transcription_corrections: Subscript ξ is very likely ρ (Z_{ρ,σ}, G_{ρ,σ}), consistent with the previous page.
'Si sa définition n'était ainsi' is likely 'Si sa définition s'avérait ainsi un peu trop limitative, ... c'est une [définition] "plus fine" qui serait la meilleure'.
